questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a pilocytic astrocytoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rosenthal fibers
  • Pilocytic astrocytoma is a low-grade glioma that is commonly found in children and young adults.
  • It is characterized by the presence of Rosenthal fibers, which are eosinophilic, elongated, and corkscrew-shaped structures. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 883

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of schwannoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: Antoni A - spindle cells are arranged in intersecting fascicles

options.label: B
options.text: Antoni B- spindle cells separated by myxoid extracellular matrix and microcyst formation

questions.solutionHtml:
Infiltrative pattern
  • The infiltrative pattern is not a feature of schwannoma.
  • Instead, schwannoma has a well-circumscribed border and tends to compress adjacent structures rather than infiltrate them.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 846

questions.stem: Which immunohistochemistry shows positive expression in schwannoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
S100
  • S100 is the immunohistochemical marker that shows positive expression in schwannoma.
  • S100 is a calcium-binding protein found in neural crest-derived cells, including Schwann cells, and is used as a diagnostic marker for various tumors derived from these cells. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 846

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common primary malignant CNS tumor in children?
questions.solutionHtml:
Medulloblastoma
  • Medulloblastoma is the most common primary malignant CNS tumor in children. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 884

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding Glioblastoma?

options.label: C
options.text: It has a high recurrence rate after treatment

questions.answerText: It has a high recurrence rate after treatment
questions.solutionHtml:
It has a high recurrence rate after treatment
  • Glioblastoma has a poor prognosis, with a high recurrence rate after treatment. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 882

questions.stemHtml: A histological section of an intracranial space-occupying lesion respected by a patient shows the findings given below. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Oligodendroglioma
  • The given clinical scenario with histological findings of “fried egg appearance” suggests the diagnosis of Oligodendroglioma.
  • The characteristic fried egg appearance refers to cells with round nuclei and clear cytoplasm that resemble fried eggs. This appearance is a hallmark of oligodendrogliomas. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 881

questions.stem: Triton tumor is a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor showing:
questions.solutionHtml:
Rhabdomyoblastic differentiation
  • Triton tumor is a rare variant of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) that shows rhabdomyoblastic differentiation.
  • Rhabdomyoblasts are skeletal muscle cells that are not typically seen in MPNST, but they are present in Triton tumors.
  • The name "Triton" comes from the Greek mythological figure who was part man and part fish, reflecting the mixed differentiation seen in this tumor. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 830

questions.stemHtml: A 68-year-old man presents with a 2-week history of tonic-clonic seizures that initially involve his left arm but have more recently progressed to involve his left leg. The cranial nerves are intact, and the Babinski sign is present. A CT scan reveals a mass in the left cerebral hemisphere. Histologic examination of the brain biopsy is shown in the image. Which of the following is the appropriate diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glioblastoma multiforme
  • The given clinical history with a histological image showing pseudo-palisading pleomorphic tumor cells suggests the diagnosis of Glioblastoma multiforme. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 881
